title: Sigil and Crown
premise: Felix Ravensworth, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has survived the collapse of the kingdom of Thornfell by staying invisible—until the old gods, silent for a century, begin answering prayers again and mark Felix as their doorkeeper. Hunted by the Regent's inquisitors who want to control the returning gods, and guided by a dead smuggler-queen whose bones Felix carries, they must retrace every hidden road through the mountains to find the Threshold, the last true door out of a country that officially no longer exists. In the end Felix learns the door opens only for someone willing to give up their name entirely—and chooses instead to become the door itself, letting the refugees of Thornfell pass through while remaining behind as its living keeper.
about_author: Noor Zhou is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice who grew up in border towns that changed hands three times in one generation. They write fantasy about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Listening Trade
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the smuggler town of Ashmoor, Felix carves messages into bone so the dead can speak to paying clients, hiding their gift behind artisan respectability. A desperate woman asks Felix to contact her son, killed by the Regent's men. The beat: quiet complicity—the cost of staying neutral.

chapters.title: What the Bones Said
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The dead boy's voice comes through wrong: not grief but a warning—'the gods are waking, and they know your hands.' That night, Felix's carved sigils glow without being asked. The beat: dread; invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: The Queen in the Satchel
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix consults their most prized relic: the fingerbones of Vessa Marrow, the smuggler-queen who once mapped every pass out of Thornfell. Vessa's ghost wakes fully for the first time in years, sharp-tongued and terrified. The beat: an unlikely alliance forms.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Vance's POV. Vance investigates a village where a drowned child walked out of a river alive after prayers to a forgotten god. She finds a bone sigil bearing Felix's maker's mark. The beat: cold purpose—the hunt begins.

chapters.title: Ashmoor Burns
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inquisitors raid Ashmoor seeking the 'god-speaker.' Felix escapes through the tannery tunnels with Vessa's satchel, leaving clients and friends behind. The beat: guilt and survival; neutrality was always an illusion.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: New character POV: Wren, a teenage guide who knows the high passes, catches Felix on the mountain trail and demands passage money—or partnership. The beat: grudging trust; Felix gains a witness to their humanity.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Vessa reveals the truth: the Threshold, the door out of Thornfell, can only be found by someone carrying both her bones and a god's attention. The old gods aren't waking randomly—they're calling Felix home. The beat: revelation reframes the flight as a summons.

chapters.title: The Regent's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. The Regent offers Vance a title if she captures the god-speaker alive; the crown wants to own the returning gods as weapons. Vance hesitates, remembering the resurrected child's eyes. The beat: first crack in her certainty.

chapters.title: Salt Shrine
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sheltering in a cliff shrine, Wren watches Felix bargain with a minor river god who demands a memory as toll. Felix pays with the memory of their mother's face. The beat: awe and fear—power always collects.

chapters.title: The Company of the Missing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Refugees from burned villages join the trek, believing Felix leads them to safety. Felix never promised anything, yet cannot turn them away. The beat: reluctant leadership; identity shifting from fugitive to shepherd.

chapters.title: Vance Closes In
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. She interrogates a captured refugee and realizes Felix is protecting civilians, not hoarding power. She falsifies her report to buy time—a betrayal of the Regent she can't undo. The beat: moral turn; justice diverges from law.

chapters.title: The Pass of Names
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At a mountain pass where the kingdom's boundary stones lie toppled, the dead of Thornfell's wars rise to bar the way, demanding to be remembered. Felix carves each name into bone through the night. The beat: exhaustion transfigured into ritual; memory as payment.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers Felix's deepest secret: they were born in the palace as the Regent's sibling, erased from record after refusing a blood rite. Confrontation in the snow. The beat: betrayal and forgiveness; identity as chosen, not given.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The mountain's eldest god offers Felix a shortcut to the Threshold—in exchange for Wren, whose bloodline once served it. Felix refuses, sealing the pass with an avalanche. The beat: defining refusal; power declined at real cost.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Choice
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. The Regent, learning of Vance's false report, sends executioners after her too. Vance finds Felix's camp and, instead of arresting them, warns them of the trap ahead. The beat: alliance of the hunted.

chapters.title: The Doorless Country
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The company reaches the valley where the Threshold should be and finds only open meadow—the country's erasure consumed the door. Despair spreads; some refugees turn back toward the Regent's amnesty. The beat: darkest hour; hope must be rebuilt from nothing.

chapters.title: Vessa's Last Map
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Vessa confesses she died at the Threshold a century ago, refused entry because she wouldn't surrender her name and legend. Her map was never of roads—it was of herself. The beat: devastating clarity; the door was always a sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Naming Rite
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. At the meadow, the waking gods gather. To open the Threshold, someone must give up their name, history, and self—becoming unrecorded, like the country itself. Felix volunteers before anyone else can. The beat: terrible resolve.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, dissolving. As Felix's name unravels, the Threshold tears open in the meadow light. Vance holds back the Regent's arriving soldiers alone; Wren leads the refugees through. The beat: climax—sacrifice made visible, love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the far side, Wren looks back: Felix remains as the living door, nameless and luminous, and the meadow closes behind the last refugee. The beat: grief braided with peace; the price honored.

chapters.title: A Country That Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. The Regent falls when his soldiers, passing through the open door's edge, remember their own erased histories and refuse his orders. Vance burns the god-speaker file and walks into the mountains. The beat: justice achieved outside the law.

chapters.title: Sigil and Crown
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Years later, Wren carves bone sigils in a free settlement, teaching children the names of the dead—including, at last, a new name whispered to the door: not Felix Ravensworth's old one, but one freely given back. The beat: resolution—identity restored by choice, the crown remembered only as a cautionary tale.
